Theorem
[Volume bounds the number of cusp ends] Source: chow-et-al-ricci-flow-part-iv:page-0212 1. ch31:31.46\group Hyperbolic cusps

If a finite-volume hyperbolic 3-manifold has $m$ cusp ends, then $\operatorname {Vol}(\mathcal H)\ge m u $, where $ u $ is the volume of the regular ideal tetrahedron; moreover it contains $m$ disjoint cusp ends each of volume at least $\sqrt3/4$.
